analysis: This batch contains only documentation: a new changelog fragment (changelog.d/ssd-eviction-selection.md, lines 1-10) and an added paragraph in docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md (head lines ~531-546) plus a date bump on line 3. No executable source is supplied, so the SSD eviction implementation (SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.evictOldest, SSDBlockIndex.oldest, oldestFirstSnapshot) was not reviewed. The docs describe a change in how LRU victims are selected: one linear probe first, then a heap-based snapshot only if the first file is busy or cannot be unlinked. They state that file leases, epoch validation, the store's removal lock and reconciliation back to the disk budget still govern retirement. Relevant threat: T-041 (prefix-cache at-rest tier). T-041 relies on a 30-minute sliding TTL, an LRU disk budget that unlinks oldest-by-last-hit, and epoch stability. The documented behavior keeps the LRU order for stable indexes and bounds the pass, so it does not contradict those mitigations. The docs do admit that concurrent schedules can pick different victims from a pre-attempt snapshot; that affects eviction ordering, not confidentiality or tenant isolation. Remaining questions for deeper source review: whether the snapshot can pick an entry replaced or touched mid-pass and unlink a newer file (the docs say lease and epoch validation guard this), whether the bounded pass still enforces the disk budget when many files are busy or undeletable, and whether TTL sweeps are unaffected. These claims are unverified here because the implementation was not supplied. No new attack surface or threat-model gap was identified from the documentation alone.
